While I think the math is fun that they found, it's equivalent to begging the question. Assuming a spherical wavefunction (which contains pi) there's a way to approximate energy states. Turns out that same approximation can recover pi. Think about it like this, an ionized hydrogen atom (aka proton) is spherical. This spherical symmetry is one of the determining factors of the energy states. So, one can use the energy state approximation of this spherical constraint to recover pi. Flatten it all down into 2-d, and simplify the higher math and you have, "Formula for pi found in circle."

"Just a quirk. The process is kind of rigged when they introduce their variational wavefunction.
